SMTO-PRX-0003 — SMTO filled in a Proxmox request incorrectly

GUID: 8dfbac69-32e6-44d8-b4b9-ad5b4ecab31c
Slug: proxmox-arguments-invalid
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO tried to run a Proxmox action, but some details it filled in were missing or in the wrong form. Nothing was sent to Proxmox.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let SMTO read the problem and correct its request; it usually does this by itself. The error tells SMTO which detail didn't fit.
  2. If it keeps failing, tell SMTO the exact node name and machine ID, the number shown next to the machine in the Proxmox web interface. Most Proxmox actions need these, and guessing them leads to this error.
  3. Make sure any values you asked for, such as memory size or number of CPUs, are plain numbers. Proxmox rejects words or units where it expects a number.

What success looks like

  • SMTO runs the Proxmox action and reports its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will be rejected the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Proxmox endpoint execution rejected the parameters because they do not satisfy the selected endpoint's generated schema, or a multipart upload lacked a granted upload_context_id.

What this means

  • Endpoint execution validates supplied params against the selected endpoint's JSON schema and rejects a mismatch. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • Endpoint execution validates supplied params against the selected endpoint's JSON schema and rejects a mismatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the named endpoint, parameter types and constraints before changing server settings.

How to fix it

  • Correct the parameters against the endpoint's generated schema (required path parameters such as node and vmid, field types and ranges) and resubmit. Multipart uploads also require a granted upload_context_id.
  • Correct the named fields, types and ranges against the advertised operation schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended endpoint parameters validate before resource dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
